endorsements.quote: Based on our experience, this step should precede larger-scale deployment and ideally involve 5-10 representative students to capture diverse interactions with the VR environment.

Identifying curricular gaps before integrating VR into medical education is crucial to ensure that the technology is applied strategically, targeting specific deficiencies in the current curriculum that are difficult or impossible to address with traditional learning methods.
Project goals and milestones must be clearly defined to ensure structured progress.
Early engagement and walkthroughs with end users help identify practical challenges and inform iterative improvements.

unlisted_practices: Justify the added educational value of VR over other teaching methods before adopting it.
Assemble an interdisciplinary consortium combining medical didactics, computer science, and design expertise.
Define learning objectives aligned with competency-based frameworks before developing scenarios.
Conduct iterative development with regular feedback from medical experts, educators, and students.
Have medical experts manually check AI-generated content for correctness and unrealistic artifacts.
Design AI integration flexibly to allow short-term adjustments as the technology evolves.
Provide alternative learning options for students experiencing cybersickness.
Provide a VR tutorial so users learn the controls before the simulation.
Establish a central technical coordinator for multisite development projects.
Define roles and responsibilities using a RACI matrix and review it at each milestone.
Use a shared cloud platform that complies with national data protection regulations for sensitive data.
Disseminate findings through open-access publications, project websites, and professional networking.
Review asset licensing early and plan post-project ownership and maintenance for sustainability.
Use an agile project management framework such as Scrum with Kanban tools.
Design a blended learning structure in which theoretical input precedes VR simulation.

screen.reason: The paper is a tutorial and implementation guideline presenting recommendations and best practices from a project on developing AI-supported virtual reality training courses for medical education.
